newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's insurance market passes key solvency test.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's insurance market passes key solvency test.

text.p: Insurance market Lloyd's of London said on Friday it had met its global solvency margin needs and added that returns to Britain's Department of Trade and Industry showed that the required miminum solvency margin had been covered 5.1 times for 1995.

Lloyd's, which secured British government backing for its crucial recovery plan this week, said the solvency margin had improved from 3.9 times at the end of 1994 and from 3.0 times at the end of 1993.

"Against the background of the successful completion of our reconstruction and renewal programme we look forward with renewed confidence to meeting the insurance needs of our customers worldwide," Lloyd's chairman David Rowland said in a statement.
"They will be encouraged as we are by the sharp improvement in the overall solvency level of the market," he added.
The solvency margin is a measure of Lloyd's financial strength and its ability to carry on paying claims. All insurers have to pass DTI solvency tests, which examine their assets every year.

The solvency test was the next key development in finalising the market's 3.2 billion pounds ($5.02 billion) recovery plan following government approval earlier this week and overwhelming acceptance of the plan by Lloyd's members, or Names.
